Deep Lindsey extends the original one-step look-ahead to three steps, balancing computational tractability against optimality. The Half Game Manager and Pseudo-Full Game Manager exploit conditional independence under a runs-based objective to drastically reduce state-space complexity, enabling faster simulation but potentially losing score-dependent strategic nuances. Suboptimal Cost quantifies how far actual managerial decisions deviate from the Lindsey-optimal path, providing an empirical metric to assess real-world coaching effectiveness. Together, these primitives form a rigorous experimental pipeline: generate diverse AI opponents with varying levels of optimality and computational efficiency, measure their performance relative to human managers using suboptimal cost as a loss function, and validate the Lindseys approach through large-scale simulation.
